text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN
- Private sector shipowners urged the government to remove restrictions on shipping services to India and allow them to load cargoes from Indian ports for third countries.
- Pakistan's cotton and textile sector is losing foreign exchange of $1.2 billion annually by not following the cotton standards prescribed by the Pakistan Cotton Standard Institute.
- A shipbreakers' strike, which entered its 22nd day on Wednesday, has severely hit a chain of Pakistani units making iron and steel products from scrap, owners say.
- The Privatisation Commission has offered six state-owned vegetable oil processing units for sale in open auction.
- The Prime Minister's secretariat has told the Central Board of Revenue to provide details of sales tax evasion.
- The federal government told provincial governments that it could not remain indifferent to deteriorating law and order.
- A cholera outbreak in Sargodha has killed 11 people. At least 42 people have been hospitalised.
- At least 11 people died and scores were injured in two separate incidents of terrorism in Lahore and Multan.
- Ayaz Baloch, a Drug Enforcement Agency employee at the U.S. embassy, arrested on charges of drug smuggling, will be tried by a military court, the Pakistan Air Force said.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- The government will provide 30 billion rupees of credit to farmers, compared to 14 billion last year, and will ensure that 80 percent of the additional credit goes to small farmers.
FINANCIAL POST
- Sindh province farmers board has expressed grave concern over a government decision to allow imports of cotton, sugar and chillies from India.
THE NEWS
- The production of crude oil has dropped from 29,000 barrels per day to 21,000 bpd in the last 15 months.
- Chinese Vice Foreign Minister Tang Jiaxuan called on President Farooq Leghari.
THE MUSLIM
- Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohammad will visit Pakistan in November along with a delegation of investors.
